messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — starting a phased rollout for telemetry sampling consent in the Python SDK. goal is: respect user consent flags, avoid surprising quota attribution, and give console a clean toggle for ‘consent-aware sampling’.
kevin: high level — is this opt-in or opt-out for existing customers?
sarah: from UX POV we should default to current behaviour for existing customers (so opt-out of new opt-in behavior), but expose a clear migration flag. we can label it in console as ‘consent-aware sampling (beta)’.
maria: agreed on default. plan is: new SDKs will expose `consent_sampling=True` but only enabled for new installs. existing installs keep old semantics. we’ll ship a server-side header switch so routing can strip/interpret consent.
tim: can you paste the client-side API? want to validate with the go/ts SDK leads.
maria: example —```
# python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'), telemetry_sampling='consent')
# valid values: 'always', 'none', 'consent'
```
josh: what happens to quota accounting? if users opt out of telemetry, will console still attribute quota properly? need to avoid undercounting.
sarah: console team: we’ll add a best-effort attribution path: if telemetry is suppressed we’ll fall back to route-level aggregation by token metrics from the ingestion proxy. it’ll be marked as ‘estimated’ in the dashboard.
kevin: ops question — does the sampling consent change request headers? we should standardize a header name, otherwise SDKs diverge. proposal: `X-RW-TELEMETRY-CONSENT: consent|no-consent|always`
maria: liking the header. SDK will send it when telemetry_sampling != 'always'. server will honor, but we’ll also have a server-side opt-in override for enterprise switches.
tim: compatibility — older SDKs won’t send header. server should treat absence as previous default behaviour (send telemetry). confirm?
maria: yes. absence => telemetry preserved (so existing customers unchanged). new behavior requires explicit SDK field or env var `RW_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=consent`.
josh: any impact to quota enforcement? e.g., per-tenant burst protections rely on granular telemetry. if telemetry goes away, risk of noisy tenants. ops/infra needs a fallback.
eke: (typo) ops ping —
kevin: infra note — we’ll implement a conservative fallback: if telemetry omitted for >5% of requests in a tenant window, mark tenant for strict rate limiting until we reconcile. but we should avoid false positives. propose a 1h smoothing window.
sarah: dashboard changes: we’ll add an indicator on tenant overview: ‘telemetry coverage: 87% (estimated contributions shown)’. and a toggle to show/hide estimated data.
maria: rollout stages: 1) canary SDK build: telemetry header + env var, server accepts header but no behavioral change. 2) console tile for opt-in preview + estimated attribution. 3) enable opt-in default for new installs only. 4) enterprise knob for account-wide opt-out. timeline: 3 weeks with telemetry canary.
deploy-bot: py-sdk 1.14.0-canary deployed to canary orgs at 2026-03-23T15:02:00Z
tim: will add a short migration guide in devex repo and update changelog. also need tests: header present, header absent, and server fallback for missing telemetry.
maria: tests planned. also adding e2e that simulates suppressed telemetry and checks console shows estimated attribution flag.
josh: one more ask — add an admin warning email template for accounts that flip to consent-aware sampling (enterprise) because support will field calls.
sarah: happy to draft copy.
kevin: permission model — customers using RW_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=consent might need updated TOS? legal to confirm.
maria: putting legal on loop.
kevin: ok good. one annoyance: some internal SDK helpers re-use the generic `telemetry` boolean. will need small breaking change to accept string enum. we should bump minor and include clear deprecation warnings.
maria: yep — will surface a deprecation warning at import if boolean used: `DeprecationWarning: telemetry bool is deprecated, use telemetry_sampling='always'|'none'|'consent'`. we’ll provide a compatibility shim for 2 releases.
tim: Can we add a quick lint rule in CI to catch boolean usage? makes rollout safer.
maria: will add.
sarah: any objections to the above plan?
josh: none from support. sounds reasonable.
kevin: approved. timeline OK. will sync with eng-platform on header naming and server flags.
maria: thanks all — posting the canary link and the draft migration doc in #devex-resources after this thread.
